## Methods - LLM benchmarking

LLMs are conventional wisdom generators. Like your ensemble, they should do better at neoclassical & green growth than post-growth (even humans are pretty fuzzy on both, especially the post/degrowth), right?

::: {.callout-caution}
"run-to-run variance in GPT-4o output"

## Findings

Green growth and Neoclassical only co-occur 6% of the time. 

Neoclassical falls from 50% in 1995 to 3% in 2019, and recovers to 8% by 2020

Post-Growth becomes most common (25%)!

## Next steps 

Co-occurrence of paradigms with 

- How bad?
- Who decides? 
- What to do? 
    - mitigation (taxes, subsidies)
    - adaptation/resilience (green, grey, behavioral)
    - compensation (types of loss and damage)
    - relocation/migration (aid, restrict)
    
This will add richness & clarify what paradigms imply. 

## Next steps 

Co-occurrence of paradigms with other paradigms (Meckling and Allan's is not the only one)

- Cashore and Bernstein (2023) "commons (Type 1), economic optimization (Type 2), compromise (Type 3), and prioritization (Type 4)" 
- "Deep green"
- etc.

This will add richness & clarify what paradigms imply.

It will also help you speak to more scholarly and practitioner communities.

## Small notes 

- Table 2 is hard to comprehend, since it is in percentage terms for the whole time period 
- "an exact match rate of 0.64" among models or with humans?
- If appendices are diluting the signal, why don't you remove them (it's only 1k documents; you can do a lot by hand)
- If classification is at the paragraph-level, be careful about saying "document." If classification is at the document level, why not paragraphs?  This is confusing, especially the part about secondary tags. 

> "Where a **document** exceeded 0.7 on at least one label, secondary and tertiary labels
were assigned at a relaxed threshold of 0.6, on the grounds that confirmed paradigmatic content
raises the prior probability of additional paradigmatic framing elsewhere in the **same document**."
